id_and_class.theory_title: Indian Personal Consciousness: Plural Selves and Real Matter
id_and_class.summary: A minority of Indian traditions (Sāṃkhya and Yoga, Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika, Jainism, and the theistic Vedāntas of Rāmānuja, Madhva, and Chaitanya) hold that conscious selves are irreducibly many and matter is irreducibly real. They reject both Advaitic moves: reducing matter to an appearance in consciousness, and treating many subjects as one subject misperceived. In liberation the individual center of experience survives as an individual.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Many Eternal Selves in Real Matter

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness belongs to individual selves that are eternal existents in their own right. It is the essence of the self for Sāṃkhya, Jainism, and the Vedāntas, and an adventitious quality of the self for Nyāya.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Several schools place the whole cognitive apparatus (intellect, ego, mind, memory, emotion) on the material side and reserve phenomenality for the self. Swami Medhananda describes the body and brain as gross matter, the mind as subtle matter, and the soul as what illuminates the mind with consciousness.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (Sāṃkhya argues that an effect pre-exists in its cause, so insentient matter can never yield sentience; Nyāya is the exception, treating consciousness as a quality that arises in the self under bodily conditions)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Phenomenal consciousness is first-personal and intrinsically many. Rāmānuja separates the self, which is consciousness by nature, from attributive consciousness that streams outward to illuminate objects, as light belongs to a lamp.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: In Sāṃkhya, mind and its contents are insentient and appear conscious only by reflecting the light of puruṣa.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Infinitely or innumerably many eternal selves (puruṣa, ātman, jīva); real matter (prakṛti, ajīva, karmic matter); in the theistic Vedāntas, a God on whom selves depend.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Scriptural reasoning, inference, and meditative and spiritual experience, whose epistemic credentials Swami Medhananda wants philosophy of mind to take seriously.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Gross body, subtle mind, and conscious self. The details vary: Jainism divides reality into sentient jīva and insentient ajīva; Madhva asserts a fivefold difference among God, souls, and matter; the Gauḍīya school holds the soul to be simultaneously one with and distinct from God.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; Personal identity and individuation; Liberation and rebirth
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: A dualism drawn between consciousness and mind rather than between mind and body (Sāṃkhya), combined with a defense of the plurality of subjects. Swami Medhananda, following the Ramakrishna tradition, adds that ‘the one divine consciousness playfully limits itself’ as each person’s private consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Individual selves pass through many cycles of birth, death, and rebirth. Liberation is isolation, eternal proximity to God, or the unobstructed exercise of the soul’s own faculties, never absorption into a cosmic whole.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In Jainism, jīva extends to plants, microorganisms, and elemental beings and adapts to the size of its body; Nyāya’s self is all-pervading.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Jainism holds that karmic matter genuinely binds to the soul and obscures its infinite knowledge, perception, bliss, and energy. In Sāṃkhya, spirit and matter stay in mere proximity, and bondage is misidentification.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Sāṃkhya’s internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa) comprises thinking, will or intellect, ego, and the substance through which they act; all of it reflects the sentience of puruṣa.
core_claims_and_evidence: Matter is real and independent of consciousness, so the problem of how an insentient world is experienced by a sentient self returns in full.
Since an effect pre-exists in its cause, no arrangement of insentient matter can produce sentience.
The plurality of subjects follows from the different births, deaths, and psychological histories of individuals.
The Bhagavad Gita calls the embodied self an eternal portion (aṃśa) of the divine, which the theistic Vedāntas interpret in different ways.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and scriptural argument, supplemented by meditative and spiritual experience.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Sāṃkhya’s conjunction of two principles defined to exclude interaction is asserted rather than derived, and its reflection metaphor redescribes the appearance it should explain. Nyāya’s view entails that liberated selves are unconscious, which few accepted. Advaita critics held that the plurality argument shows only apparent plurality, and asked what distinguishes one contentless witness from another.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The theistic Vedāntas solve individuation by appeal to divine agency, so their account rests on a theological premise. How contentless selves differ from one another remains open.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Each school is internally rigorous, but the family is not one doctrine. Schweizer argues the Sāṃkhya split gives cognitive science its whole domain while isolating phenomenality, an advantage over Cartesian dualism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since mind and matter are insentient and consciousness belongs only to eternal selves, building a machine would not create a new conscious subject.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Selves are eternal, reincarnate through many lives, and survive liberation as individuals.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Each tradition frames life as a path to liberation, whether as isolation, purification from karma, or eternal relation to God.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A digital copy would reproduce only material, insentient processes, not the self that experiences them.
